forces: The sanctioned merge path decides what enters the protected branch, yet it lived outside the repository with no tests and behind no required check, so two defects shipped in it undetected.
A merge gate whose logic can only run against live GitHub state is exercised only on inputs that happen to occur, and neither observed defect occurs on a healthy pull request.
gh pr checks --required lists only contexts that have reported, so counting not-passing over that list settles on an incomplete set and a context that never started reads as absent-and-fine.

A squash replays a branch as one commit parented on the target tip, orphaning any commit a governance record binds, so selecting the merge method by inspecting pull request contents can pick a method that breaks check-governance-history.
CI names one repository script test file by hand rather than enumerating them, so npm-audit-retry.test.mjs was written, passes, and is executed by no check at all.

approach-new-required-merge-gate-context.reason: Pinning a new required context makes every open pull request unmergeable until it re-runs, and the existing design-pattern-governance context already runs node --test over repository script and governance test directories.

evidence_ids: merge-gate.mjs holds every decision as a function over supplied evidence and imports only node:fs and node:url; merge-pr.sh collects evidence and delegates the judgment
evaluateRequiredChecks reads the protected branch required-context list and reports never-reported and not-passing distinctly; the PR #245 shape and its null control are both asserted
selectMergeMethod returns --merge for every pull request, records the archive reason without selecting on it, and refuses a pull request reporting no changed paths
the design-pattern-governance job runs node --test .github/scripts/*.test.mjs, executing merge-gate.test.mjs and the previously unrun npm-audit-retry.test.mjs
